transcribed_question: A) IDENTIFY THE STRUCTURE LABELLED A B) IDENTIFY THE STRUCTURE LABELLED B

marker.description: Label A pointing to the oocyte

main_explanation: Label A points to the large central cell within the antral follicle, which is the oocyte.

supporting_question.question: Which of the following hormones is primarily responsible for stimulating the growth of ovarian follicles?
supporting_question.explanation: FSH (Follicle-Stimulating Hormone) is the primary hormone responsible for initiating and supporting the growth and development of ovarian follicles.

true_false.statement: The presence of an antrum is characteristic of a primordial follicle.
true_false.explanation: The antrum is a fluid-filled cavity that develops within secondary (antral) and mature (Graafian) follicles. Primordial follicles are the earliest stage and do not possess an antrum.
